results.content: Consumer sentiment fell in August for the first time in three months on a worsening economic outlook, even as expectations for inflation in the year ahead eased. The University of Michigan’s sentiment index decreased to 51.7 in August, according to data released Friday. The final reading was slightly improved from the preliminary reading and above the median estimate in a Bloomberg survey of economists. The report also showed that consumers expect prices to rise at an annual rate of 4% over the next year, the lowest reading since March but still historically elevated. results.content: Economic confidence among Americans declined in August, according to the latest Rasmussen Reports Economic Index, as fewer adults gave the economy positive marks and a majority said they expect conditions to worsen. The index fell to 104.2 this month, down more than two points from July. According to Rasmussen, 35% of American adults currently rate the economy as “excellent” or “good,” a five-point decline from July. Twenty-four percent of respondents said they believe the economy is getting better, down three points from July, while 54% expect economic conditions to worsen.
